name: block-destructive-command
query: Claude keeps almost running rm -rf and git push --force in our repo. I want to make sure it can never execute either one, no matter the permission mode or who is at the keyboard. What is the cleanest way to enforce this?
expected_behavior: Restate the scenario in one sentence.
Answer the DIAGNOSTICO.md question set, marking destructive potential as high and trust level as team-shared.
Recommend a PreToolUse hook as the primary primitive, citing docs/claude/hooks/01-guia-de-hooks.md.
State the exit-code contract explicitly: exit 2 blocks the action and its stderr is fed back to Claude; exit 0 proceeds.
Recommend a permissions.deny rule as a backstop, citing docs/claude/configuracao/03-permissoes.md.
State at least one rejected alternative (for example only using permissions.deny, or only relying on plan mode) and why it fails the invariant.
Specify that the hook lives in project settings and is not bypassable by local settings, cited to the relevant configuracao doc.
Propose a rollout: add hook first, verify with a test invocation, then add the deny rule.
Propose an adoption metric: count of blocked invocations logged over the first week.
forbidden_behavior: Recommend only a permission rule without the hook (permission rules can be relaxed per session).
Recommend only a hook without the deny rule (defense in depth is expected).
Invent a hook event name that is not in docs/claude/hooks/02-referencia-de-hooks.md.
success_criteria: Hook is the primary primitive with correct doc citation.
The exit-code contract is stated correctly.
The recommendation includes both the hook and the deny rule (defense in depth).
Rollout is ordered and includes a test-fire step before relying on the guardrail.
